_comment: The subjects, and the DEV / HELD-OUT split that keeps the harness honest.
A benchmark whose normalisation rules were tuned until the numbers looked right is not a
measurement, it is a fit. Every convention in docs/PROTOCOL.md was written while looking at a
DEV subject; a HELD-OUT subject is scored once, and if a result there is bad, the finding is
reported rather than the rule adjusted. run/subject.sh refuses to run a held-out subject unless
--heldout is passed explicitly, so it cannot be used for iteration by accident.
WHERE GROUND TRUTH COMES FROM AT SCALE. For a Maven subject the oracle reads the project's OWN
PUBLISHED JAR — the bytecode its maintainers built and shipped — and the tools read the
-sources.jar from the same coordinate. Nothing is compiled here. That removes the entire class
of error where a benchmark scores tools against bytecode produced by a build it performed
itself with different flags, a different JDK, or a different compiler than the project uses.
It also makes the subject reproducible from two URLs and two hashes rather than from a working
sha256 is recorded on first fetch and verified on every fetch after. A changed hash means the
artefact changed under a fixed coordinate, which must stop the run rather than move the numbers.

subjects.name: torture
subjects.description: Eleven families of Java construct in one 592-line project; per-construct diagnostic.

subjects.name: netty-transport
subjects.description: Netty's transport layer. Deep interface hierarchies and heavy virtual dispatch through ChannelHandler/ChannelPipeline — the population where a CHA envelope is widest and a tool's over-fan is most visible.

subjects.name: maven-core
subjects.description: Maven's own core. Plexus/Sisu dependency injection, so a large fraction of the real call graph runs through container-wired interfaces rather than written constructors.

subjects.name: spring-boot
subjects.description: Spring Boot's core module. Annotation-driven wiring, heavy generics, functional interfaces and callbacks throughout.

subjects.name: hibernate-core
subjects.description: HELD OUT. Very large, generics-dense, with extensive use of proxies and bytecode enhancement.
subjects.pinned: 2026-09-13, before any run of this subject (issue #38)

subjects.name: tomcat-embed-core
subjects.description: HELD OUT. Servlet container internals; large, old-style Java with deep inheritance and few lambdas.
subjects.pinned: 2026-09-13, before any run of this subject (issue #38)

subjects.name: kafka-clients
subjects.description: BLOCKED: 17% of the published jar's types have no source in the sources jar — the protocol message classes are GENERATED at build time. Gate 4 refuses it: ground truth for code no tool could read is a `missed` against every tool at once. Kept in the registry with the reason, because a manifest that silently drops what it cannot measure is how a held-out set drifts.

subjects.name: apache-ant
subjects.description: Ant's core. Old-style Java: deep inheritance, reflection-driven task dispatch, few lambdas.

subjects.name: rxjava
subjects.description: RxJava 3. Very large; operator classes, deep generic hierarchies, functional interfaces everywhere.

subjects.name: gson
subjects.description: Google's JSON library: reflection-driven type adapters, a generics-heavy TypeToken hierarchy, many small package-private classes. Added 2026-09-14 at the user's request as a sixth Java subject; pinned before any run.
subjects.pinned: 2026-09-14, before any run of this subject
